provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1862 reads `beatum Paschd lem Confess6rem` where the 1962 reads `PTHVeus quibeatumPaschalemCon JL fessorem`; the 1862 reads `C6rporis` where the 1962 reads `Corporis` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `noc` where the 1962 reads `hoc` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `convfvio` where the 1962 reads `convivio` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `pinguedinem edm dem` where the 1962 reads `pingu dinem eandem`; 6 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1922 Mame reads `dilectiéne` where the 1962 reads `dilectione` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1922 Mame reads `hoe` where the 1962 reads `hoc`; 3 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1922 Mame prints the conclusion as `Qui vivis DIE 18 MAJI SANCTI VENANTII MARTYRIS` where the 1962 prints `Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre`. Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 597 (artifact PDF p. 711), target-body character coverage 0.95, found by a sweep; Benziger 1962 conformed printing, target-body character coverage 0.87. Recorded limitation: The 1962 prints this under 05-17 with the rubric Commune Sanctorum [24]. Every 1862 reading here rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone; this lane has no page image of the 1862, and the recogniser damages roughly one word in three there, so where the 1862's letterforms differ from the 1962's the difference recorded above is an inference from the layer and not a reading of the leaf. The 1922 Mame is the check on those places, and it is a full public-domain peer rather than mere corroboration. Not checked: the 1962 page image for this oration, the 1570 (its recogniser is too degraded to control a claim), and the 1604 except where named. || REPAIRED by lane repair-2 on 2026-09-03. The stored target had been a text-layer reading carrying recogniser damage; it has been replaced word for word by a reading taken from the 1962 CMAA facsimile page image at 400 dpi (artifact PDF p. 613, printed folio read on the same image). Line-end hyphens are joined, printed stress accents are dropped, and the ae/oe ligatures are expanded to two letters; punctuation, capitalisation and the conclusion are reproduced at the length the page prints them. The verdict, the antecedent locus and the recorded differences are the original lane's and were not revisited. The marginal number 2615 already in the locus was confirmed on the same 400 dpi image. This page's printed folio is absent from the CMAA text layer, so it was read directly on a 300 dpi rendering of the head of artifact PDF p. 613, where it prints 532; the printed-page/PDF-page offset of 81 therefore holds here as elsewhere. The conclusion is printed at the length reproduced here, ending at Deo Patre without the further clause.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui beatum Paschalem Confessorem tuum mirifica erga Corporis et
Sanguinis tui sacra mysteria dilectione decorasti: concede propitius; ut,
quam ille ex hoc divino convivio spiritus percepit pinguedinem, eandem et
nos percipere mereamur: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
